02 — MAC INTEGRATION

Use the menu bar.
Automate settings.

OpenXM runs as a native Mac app. Check battery levels, change settings, and apply scenes from the menu bar or with keyboard shortcuts.

View keyboard shortcuts ↗
⌘

Menu bar controls

View battery status and change noise mode, EQ, or scenes without opening the main window.

↻

Automatic scenes

Apply saved settings when headphones connect, on a schedule, or when an app opens. Launch at login is optional.

✓

Setting verification

OpenXM reads settings back from the headphones where supported. The Activity view shows which changes were confirmed, adjusted, or failed.

03 — COMPATIBILITY

Which headphones
does it support?

The main targets are WH-1000XM3 and WH-1000XM4. Available controls depend on the model and firmware. Hardware testing of this project is still pending.

HEADPHONESSTATUSWHAT TO EXPECT
WH-1000XM4Primary target

The upstream project tested XM4 controls. Hardware testing of OpenXM is pending.

WH-1000XM3Primary target

Uses the same protocol generation as XM4. Hardware testing of OpenXM is pending.

WH-1000XM5 / XM6Experimental

Protocol support is included. Not verified on hardware in this project.

Feature availability varies by model and firmware. XM3 does not have Speak-to-Chat. No firmware updates or extra macOS audio codecs. See the full compatibility notes ↗

PRIVACY & SOURCE CODE

No account.
No analytics.

Headphone commands go over Bluetooth. Scenes and preferences are stored on your Mac. Optional update checks contact GitHub and are off by default. The code is MIT licensed: inspect it, modify it, or build it yourself.

View source on GitHub ↗

04 — INSTALLATION

Install OpenXM
on your Mac.

Requires macOS 15 or newer and compatible Sony headphones paired with your Mac.

Download for Mac ↓Or build it yourself ↗

Community builds are ad-hoc signed, not notarized.
Building locally is the recommended starting point.

  1. 01

    Download and install.

    Download the archive for your Mac, unzip it, and move OpenXM.app to Applications.

  2. 02

    Connect your headphones.

    Connect your headphones in macOS Bluetooth settings, open OpenXM, and allow Bluetooth access.

  3. 03

    Change a setting.

    Choose a noise mode, adjust EQ, or save a combination of settings as a scene.

Questions & limitations

Does this install custom firmware?+

No. OpenXM changes settings through the headphones’ existing Bluetooth control protocol. It does not replace or update their firmware, unlock codecs, or change how macOS sends audio.

Does this replace the Sony phone app?+

For supported everyday controls, you can use your Mac directly. Keep the Sony app for firmware updates and features that this project does not support. No Sony account is required by OpenXM.

Does the browser preview control my headphones?+

No. It is an interactive illustration using sample data. The downloadable native Mac app communicates with headphones over Bluetooth.

Why might macOS block a download?+

Community releases use an ad-hoc signature, without paid Apple Developer ID signing or notarization. Build from source with the provided script if macOS blocks the download. You do not need to disable system security settings.

Where did this project come from?+

OpenXM is an independent MIT-licensed fork of Open Sound Connect by rolottr. Protocol references include SonyBridge and Sony Device Center. Credits and upstream license notices are preserved in the repository.
